title.en: "Firsts" are contested; landmarks are entry points

summary.en: Who invented metal or punk is not settled. Landmarks give you a dated track to start the argument from.
summary.zh: 谁发明了金属或朋克，没有定论。Landmark 给你一首带年份的歌，方便从那儿吵起。

body.en:
Ask a metal fan who started metal and you get Sabbath's tritone, earlier underground noise, or a blues bend. Everyone has a candidate. Same fight exists for punk and plenty of other tags.

Rock "firsts" are rarely clean patents. They are moments when a sound becomes hard to ignore in public, so later bands have to react.

On band pages, the Landmark card means: start here. Not "only truth," but a useful hinge—year, impact, genres it opens. On genre pages, pioneer acts are early relatives of the style, not exclusive inventors.

We keep landmarks next to stories on purpose. A separate "museum of firsts" turns into ranking fights. Next to why-it-matters copy, a debut track is something you can actually play.

Argue the genealogy later if you want. First press play on the hinge track. Then see who answered it.
body.zh:
问金属听众谁开创了金属，答案可能是 Sabbath 的三全音、更早的地下噪音，或某段 blues bend。人人都有候选人。朋克和其它标签也一样吵。

摇滚的「第一次」很少像干净专利。它们是声音在公众层面变得难忽视的节点，后面的乐队不得不回应。

乐队页的 Landmark 意思是：从这儿听起。不是「唯一真理」，而是好用的枢纽——年份、冲击、撞开的流派。流派页的开创乐队是早期亲戚，不是独家发明人。

我们故意把 landmark 放在故事旁边。单独开「第一次博物馆」容易变成排行架。贴着「为何重要」，一首首曲是你能直接按播放的东西。

谱系想吵可以稍后吵。先听枢纽那首。再看谁接了它。
